program_plain: World: a 64x64 lattice of cells (wrap-around edges, 8 neighbours each). Cells have 4 types (random start), ordered in a cycle. Rules each step, all cells at once: a cell adopts the next type in the cycle if at least 1 of its 8 neighbours already has that next type.
model_family: cellular automata / excitable media (Cyclic Cellular Automaton, Greenberg-Hastings family)
standard_name: 2-D Cyclic Cellular Automaton (range 1, Moore, threshold 1, kappa=4 or 5): locally periodic oscillation / spiral-wave regime
citations: Fisch, Gravner, Griffeath 1991, 'Cyclic Cellular Automata in Two Dimensions', Spatial Stochastic Processes (Birkhauser, Progress in Probability 19) pp.171-185 - 2-D CCA rules, asymptotic local periodicity
Fisch, Gravner, Griffeath 1991, 'Threshold-range scaling of excitable cellular automata', Statistics and Computing 1(1):23-39 - experimental threshold/range/kappa phase diagrams
Fisch, Gravner, Griffeath 1993, 'Asymptotic behavior of excitable cellular automata', Experimental Mathematics 2(3) (year from memory) - rigorous results on stable periodic objects/spirals

Shalizi & Shalizi, 'Quantifying Self-Organization in Cyclic Cellular Automata', arXiv nlin/0507067 (authors inferred from emails; year/venue not seen) - 4 colours, range-1 Moore, T=1 oscillates with period 4 per cell
Hartarsky/Foxall-type CCA-on-trees paper arXiv 2108.06404 - states that on Z^2 with theta=1 CCA fluctuates for all kappa>=3, whereas in 1-D it fixates for kappa>=5
Griffeath, 'Self-organization of random cellular automata: four snapshots' - overview of CCA/GHM family

full_text:
**Verdict: KNOWN.** The rule system is the 2-D Cyclic Cellular Automaton (CCA) with range 1, a Moore (box) neighbourhood, threshold 1, and κ = 4 or 5 colours. The observed behaviour is its standard "locally periodic" regime.

**1. Model family.** This is excitable-media cellular automata, a family that includes the Greenberg–Hastings model. In a CCA, a cell's colour advances by 1 if at least Threshold cells of the next colour are in its neighbour set. That matches your rule exactly (threshold 1, 8 neighbours, synchronous update). Griffeath's group named the family. It was discovered and explored by David Griffeath. Your rule is the (range 1, threshold 1, κ) corner of the three-parameter family studied by Fisch, Gravner and Griffeath.

**2. The specific behaviour.** I read your three features as follows:
- *Cells cycling above chance* and *activity rising* mean the lattice settles into a global periodic oscillation.
- *One cell type fills most of the lattice* is what a snapshot looks like when large single-colour regions oscillate in phase.

These are the known low-threshold behaviour, not a new effect.

- The Shalizi & Shalizi paper describes three regimes. At high thresholds the CCA freezes into static single-colour blocks. At very low thresholds the whole lattice eventually oscillates periodically, sometimes as large spiral waves that engulf it.
- For your exact setting, the paper says T=1 and T=2 are both locally oscillating with a range-one Moore neighbourhood. The paper's figures use 4 colours, a range-one box neighbourhood and random initial conditions. For its T=1 figure, the CA as a whole oscillates with period 4, each cell cycling through the colours.
- Fisch, Gravner and Griffeath proved the dynamics are not frozen. On Z² with θ = 1, the CCA fluctuates for all κ ≥ 3, via stable periodic objects (SPOs).
- This also covers your 5-type variant. In 2-D, κ = 5 is not the fixation case it is in 1-D. In 1-D with θ = 1, Fisch found the CCA almost surely fixates for κ ≥ 5 and fluctuates for κ ≤ 4. That 1-D result is the "Bob's dilemma" contrast. In 2-D the oscillation persists for κ = 5 as well.

**3. Sources.** Titles, authors and venues below are checked against the search results unless I flag otherwise.
- **Earliest clear source:** Fisch, R., Gravner, J., Griffeath, D. (1991). "Cyclic Cellular Automata in Two Dimensions." In *Spatial Stochastic Processes* (Alexander & Watkins, eds.), Birkhäuser, Progress in Probability vol. 19, pp. 171–185. It describes the dynamics of deterministic discrete-time cyclic cellular automata, which have remarkably complex dynamics. It also gives a proof of asymptotic local periodicity.
- **Companion paper (the experimental phase diagrams):** Fisch, Gravner, Griffeath (1991). "Threshold-range scaling of excitable cellular automata." *Statistics and Computing* 1(1):23–39. doi:10.1007/BF01890834. I confirmed the citation details. I only saw the paper's content through secondary descriptions.
- **Rigorous follow-up:** Fisch, Gravner, Griffeath (1993). "Asymptotic behavior of excitable cellular automata." *Experimental Mathematics* 2(3). The year is not stated in the search result, so it comes from my own knowledge. The abstract describes the earlier experimental study on Z² from random starts, and the threshold-range scaling limit.
- **Accessible review/quantification (arXiv):** Shalizi & Shalizi, "Quantifying Self-Organization in Cyclic Cellular Automata" (arXiv nlin/0507067). It gives the 4-colour, range-1 Moore T=1 case explicitly. I did not see a year or venue in the results, and I am assuming the authors from the email addresses shown (cshalizi, kshalizi). My recollection is a ~2003 SPIE proceedings, which I did not verify.
- **Short overview:** Griffeath, "Self-organization of random cellular automata: four snapshots." It describes the CCA as closely related to the Greenberg–Hastings model. The year and venue are not in the snippet.
- **Wikipedia:** the "Cyclic cellular automaton" article is a convenient summary.

**4. Differences that might matter.** Almost none.
- Your lattice is finite (64×64, wrap-around), whereas the literature is mostly on the infinite lattice. Finite size can only make a single phase or domain look more dominant. That is the likely source of your "largest domain" score, and it is not a different phenomenon.
- Your rule updates a cell when any neighbour holds the next colour, and keeps the cell's colour otherwise. This is the standard CCA update.
- Wikipedia's description of "consumption" with no threshold is the same rule at θ = 1.
- A GitHub model (cormas) uses a von Neumann neighbourhood for its standard version. That variant is not yours.

**5. Confidence: high.** The rule is identical to a named, well-studied model. Several independent sources, including a rigorous one, state the T=1 Moore, 4-colour regime as oscillatory and locally periodic. The one soft spot is that I could not read the 1991 papers' full text, only descriptions and abstracts. I also could not check the exact numeric scores from your simulation. Your quantities (cycling, domain size, activity trend) are metrics of your own, not ones the literature reports.
